site.title: Drum Town — Free Drum Lessons with Real Notation
site.description: Free drum lessons with real notation and audio playback — a full curriculum from your first backbeat to advanced vocabulary across rock, jazz, funk, Latin, fusion, metal, and hip-hop.

dock.bpm_label: BPM, tempo in beats per minute

page.lede: Every page on Drum Town carries a metronome — the tempo pill in the header opens it. Tap the pill and the controls appear across the bottom of the screen. Set a tempo, pick a time signature, and press play. This page is about using it well.
page.quick_start_desc: Tap the tempo pill in the header to open the metronome along the bottom of the screen. Type a tempo (or drag the slider), choose beats per bar — 2/4 through 7/8 — and press play. The first beat of each bar is accented so you always know where "1" is.
page.what_tempo: What Tempo Should I Practice At?
page.item_new_desc: slower than feels necessary — ♩ = 50–70. If it feels boring, it's right. (See Slow Practice.)
page.item_clean_desc: 10 BPM below the tempo where it falls apart, then move up in small steps.
page.item_speed_desc: raise the tempo ~10% only after a passage is 100% clean for two unbroken minutes.
page.three_games_desc: A click doesn't have to mark every beat. Three ways to make it harder and more useful, from Practicing with a Metronome:
page.game_2_4_desc: halve the tempo and hear the click as the backbeat. The click becomes a bandmate instead of a ruler.
page.game_bar_desc: you hold the time for three beats alone and the click grades you on beat 1.
page.game_subdiv_desc: play 8ths or 16ths against a quarter click and listen for the notes between clicks drifting.
page.dock_follow: The metronome follows you to every lesson on the site. The sound does not: a browser only lets audio start from a tap on the page you are looking at, so opening a new lesson pauses the click. The dock comes back open with your tempo and meter still set and the play button waiting — one press and it is running again.

rudiments.lede: Every one of the forty standard rudiments — rolls, paradiddles, flams, and drags — rendered as real notation. Press play to hear any of them; where we have a full lesson, it's linked right on the card.
rudiments.intro: Rudiments are to drumming what scales are to piano: small, repeatable sticking patterns that turn into fills, grooves, and solos once they're automatic. The Percussive Arts Society standardized forty of them, in the four families below. You don't need all forty at once — start with the single stroke roll, double stroke roll, and single paradiddle, then work outward. A practice pad and a metronome are all you need.
